resources.string: Redirects the Fire TV Home button to a launcher of your choice, and offers an optional long-press of the Menu key as a shortcut back into FireStick Fixer.
Your launcher: the app ⌂ Home takes you to. Press OK to choose it. Long-press OK opens its system info page.

Required for everything else in this app to work. This permission has to be granted only once via adb:\nadb shell pm grant io.github.hatim.firestickfixer android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS\nFrom a phone shell app there is no adb: run just the pm grant part, without the adb shell prefix.

A single press of ⌂ Home, from any app or from the Amazon home screen, opens your launcher instead of Amazon\'s home.\nDouble-tap ⌂ Home to stay on the Amazon home screen; a single press later takes you back to your launcher.

Pressing ⌂ Home from any third-party app opens the target app instead of the Amazon home screen.
On Fire OS 7 the system holds a Home press for up to 5 seconds; a loading animation covers the wait. A mapped launcher button that sends its own key code opens instantly instead.
Double-press ⌂ Home about a second apart, or long-press it, in the target app to escape to the Amazon home screen if needed.
Press ↩ Back or ◉ OK while the Home icon on the Amazon home screen is focused to open the target app.

On Fire OS 7 the system holds a ⌂ Home press for up to 5 seconds. This chooses what covers Amazon home during the wait. Animation plays a short loading scene. Black screen shows a plain black screen with a loading message. Fire OS 8 has no delay, so nothing is shown. Hold ◉ OK to preview the current choice.

Hold ⌂ Home to switch between your launcher and the Amazon home screen. Turn this off if you would rather see the panel that a long press opens, with its profile, sleep and mirroring tiles. Some remotes have a settings button that opens the very same panel, and FireStick Fixer cannot tell the two apart, so turning this off also stops that button from switching launchers. Press ◉ OK to switch it on or off.
Double-tap ⌂ Home to stay on the Amazon home screen. A single press of ⌂ Home later brings your launcher back. Turn this off if you never want to see Amazon\'s home. Press OK to switch it on or off.
Opens an app automatically when the Fire TV starts or wakes from standby. Move right to choose which app: your launcher (default) or any other app.
☰ Menu long-press opens this config screen
Hold the ☰ Menu button for half a second to open this config screen.

Map spare remote buttons: one for your target launcher, one for the Amazon home screen, Custom for any number of further apps. Buttons with their own key code (● ● ● ●, numbers, channel, subtitles, teletext, ⏪ ⏵ ⏩) switch instantly. Buttons that open an app (⊞ Apps, 📺 Live TV, Netflix) can only be redirected, which is slightly slower and may flash briefly.

Map spare remote buttons: one for your target launcher, one for the Amazon home screen, Custom for any number of further apps. Buttons with their own key code (● ● ● ●, numbers, channel, subtitles, teletext, ⏪ ⏵ ⏩) switch instantly, unlike ⌂ Home which Fire OS 7 holds for up to 5 seconds. Buttons that open an app (⊞ Apps, 📺 Live TV, Netflix) can only be redirected, which is slightly slower and may flash briefly.
Press ◉ OK to bind a remote button that opens your target launcher directly (↩ Back cancels); hold ◉ OK to reset.
Press ◉ OK to bind a remote button that jumps to the Amazon home screen (↩ Back cancels); hold ◉ OK to reset.
That button is already mapped to %1$s.
That button already opens this app.
Opens a dialog where further buttons can be mapped, each one to an app of your choice.

Press ◉ OK on a field to set it, hold ◉ OK to clear it. Choose the app first, then the button that should open it. A row without a button is kept but does nothing; a row without an app disappears when you close this dialog with ↩ Back.
This button opens a content app
%1$s is an app you watch, not a shell screen. Mapping its button makes %1$s unreachable everywhere, even from its own tile. Map it anyway?
That button opens an Amazon Appstore page, not an app, so there is nothing to map. If the app is not installed, install it first and try again.

That button opened the Amazon home screen, not an app, so there\'s nothing to map. Make sure the app this button should open is installed and set up so it opens when you press the button. Only then can the button be redirected.
Logs every key and window event the service receives, tagged FireStickFixer. View it on the TV with the button on the right, or from a computer with:\nadb logcat -s FireStickFixer
Open a full-screen diagnostic view (Fire OS, accessibility status, target, recent log) you can photograph and share, no adb needed.
App name, version, project link and Fire OS device info.
Sends the Fire TV ⌂ Home button to the launcher you choose, and lets you remap the remote\'s app buttons.
Run once via adb:\nadb shell pm grant io.github.hatim.firestickfixer android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS
No launchable apps found to set as target.
How soon the loading overlay covers the screen after you press ⌂ Home. Lower hides the Amazon home flash sooner. Press ◀ ▶ to change. Takes effect on Fire OS 7.

How long the overlay stays solid after the launcher window appears, before it fades. Higher gives the launcher time to draw, hiding the flash at the end. Press ◀ ▶ to change. Takes effect on Fire OS 7.
Cross-fade duration when the overlay lifts. Press ◀ ▶ to change. Takes effect on Fire OS 7.
Restore start delay %1$d ms, end hold %2$d ms, fade %3$d ms.
Hold the Menu button to open the quick menu, where this VPN is switched on or off.

Press OK to choose which installed VPN app to control. Any VPN app is listed; with only one installed it is used automatically. Hold Menu to open the quick menu; its VPN item opens this app in the background, presses connect or disconnect and returns.
Turn the chosen VPN on or off and see if it is on. Shown only when a VPN app is installed.
Opens Amazon\'s home screen once, without the launcher redirect.
A way into this settings screen from anywhere.
No search box was found, so your words were not searched. Alexa\'s own results can\'t be reopened from here.
Next time Alexa\'s results will show for %1$s. Change it in FireStick Fixer settings.
Hold Menu for the quick menu
Hold the Menu button, in any app, as long as you hold Home for its panel, to open this menu.
A short Menu press is untouched. Only a hold opens the menu, and the app underneath never sees the rest of that press.
Back does nothing on my launcher\'s main screen

Without this, ↩ Back on your launcher\'s main screen closes it and you briefly land on the Amazon home screen. Back inside the launcher\'s own menus and settings keeps working: FireStick Fixer recognises the main screen by its layout.

Active. FireStick Fixer sees every ⌂ Home press and every remote app button the moment the system handles it: Home goes straight to your launcher with no Amazon flash, double-tap is exact, and a remapped app button only fires for the button, not when you open that app yourself.

Run once from a computer (survives reboots, read-only):\nadb shell pm grant io.github.hatim.firestickfixer android.permission.READ_LOGS\nIt takes effect by itself within half a minute. Without it, FireStick Fixer falls back to slower window detection, and Amazon home can flash briefly on ⌂ Home.
Run once via adb:\nadb shell pm grant io.github.hatim.firestickfixer android.permission.READ_LOGS
Which app opens at start-up. Pick your launcher to follow it, or any other app (for example a live TV or streaming app).
Alexa voice search goes to the app I\'m in

Hold the Alexa button inside an app and speak: instead of Alexa\'s own results page, the app you were in searches for what you said. Speak from your launcher or the Amazon home screen to get Alexa\'s own results instead. Alexa commands and questions are not affected.
From a computer with adb on the same Wi-Fi (ADB debugging on in Developer Options), connect first. Each step ticks off here by itself; all of them survive reboots and updates:
Optional boosts (faster Home detection, instant app closing) show here after step 1.
Fast actions · instant app closing, Free up memory (also does 1 and 2)
Mac or Linux. Press Allow on the TV when it asks.
Press OK here to hide the optional steps. They stay in the settings below.
The app is set up. Press OK to hide the optional steps; Precise detection and Fast actions below still show how to add them.
Required · lets FireStick Fixer switch its service on
Recommended · instant ⌂ Home, exact double-tap, button-only remapping
Switch on "Accessibility service" below (it switches on by itself when 1 is done here).
Takes effect by itself within half a minute.
↩ Back: show Alexa\'s results instead · ◉ OK: search now
Lets FireStick Fixer notice Home, Back and remote buttons. Everything below needs it.
Home takes you to your launcher. Double-tap Home for Amazon\'s home screen.
Stops Back from dropping you onto Amazon\'s home screen. Menus still close.
Make a remote button open a different app, e.g. YouTube button → TizenTube.
Hold Alexa inside an app: that app searches for what you said. Back during the countdown keeps Alexa\'s results.
Faster, exact detection of Home and app buttons (one-time adb step).
Opens the chosen app when the Fire TV starts or wakes up.
Hold ↩ Back to close an app
Hold Back for a moment inside any app to jump to your launcher and close the app.

Holding ↩ Back for about 0.7 seconds inside an app takes you straight to your launcher and closes that app in the background, instead of pressing Back over and over. A short press still works as a normal Back. Not active on your launcher or Amazon\'s own screens.
FireStick Fixer: Fire OS was updated (%1$s → %2$s). Checking that everything still works.
For these apps, Alexa voice search shows Alexa\'s own results instead.

Press OK and tick as many apps as you like; OK on a ticked app unticks it. Amazon\'s own apps are ticked by default; untick any you want searched in the app. Changes save at once. Useful for apps where Alexa\'s results are better than the app\'s own search.
Amazon updates can change how Fire OS behaves. Press OK for your options.
Shows whether Amazon\'s updater is active. FireStick Fixer re-checks its features after every Fire OS update. Press OK to see how to hold updates back.

This device runs %1$s.

Amazon installs Fire OS updates automatically, and an app cannot switch that off. Two ways work:

1. Router or Pi-hole (recommended, nothing changes on the TV): block
 softwareupdates.amazon.com
 updates.amazon.com
 d1s31zyz7dcc2d.cloudfront.net
 prod.ota-cloudfront.net
 amzdigital-a.akamaihd.net
Do NOT block ftv-smtv.ntp-fireos.com (the clock needs it).

2. From a computer with adb (reversible; some builds refuse it):
 adb shell pm disable-user --user 0 com.amazon.device.software.ota
 adb shell pm disable-user --user 0 com.amazon.device.software.ota.override
 adb shell pm disable-user --user 0 com.amazon.tv.forcedotaupdater.v2
To update again: the same with "pm enable <package>", then Settings → My Fire TV → About → Check for updates.

If Fire OS does update, FireStick Fixer re-checks itself and falls back to safe behaviour where something changed.
Lets FireStick Fixer close apps instantly through the stick\'s own adb (one-time setup from a computer).

Ready. Hold Back and Free up memory close apps with a force-stop, in about a tenth of a second. While they run, wireless debugging is on for a moment and only this app\'s approved key can use it. Press OK to test.

Not set up yet. On a computer with adb, in the FireStick Fixer folder, run once:\n tools/setup-adb.sh <fire-tv-ip>\nThen press Allow on the TV when it asks. Until then, Hold Back backs out of apps instead.
This Wi-Fi isn\'t allowed for wireless debugging yet. Press OK: the TV asks "Allow wireless debugging on this network?". Tick "Always allow on this network" and press Allow.
Fast actions need ADB debugging: Settings → My Fire TV → Developer options → ADB debugging. Until then, Hold Back backs out of apps instead.
adbd no longer accepts this app\'s key (the keys were cleared). Run tools/setup-adb.sh again from a computer.
The last fast action failed: %1$s. Press OK to test again. If it keeps failing, Hold Back backs out of apps instead.
Hold ↩ Back closes the app fully
With Fast actions, hold Back force-stops the app, so it starts fresh next time.

With Fast actions ready, holding Back in an app opens your launcher and force-stops the app at once, so it starts fresh next time (apps like TizenTube otherwise reopen on their last page). Off: hold Back presses Back until the app is left, and the app keeps running in the background. System and Amazon apps are always only backed out of.
Force-stops apps running in the background (not the one on screen, not media that\'s playing, not system apps). Shown only when Fast actions are ready.
Couldn\'t free up memory: Fast actions didn\'t work. See FireStick Fixer → Fast actions.
